6.author: St. Augustine of Hippo
6.work: Tractates on the Gospel of John, Tractate 69
6.text: Augustine reads 'I am the way, the truth, and the life' as a single saying, not a list of three claims. Christ is the way because He is the truth and the life. Truth without a road to it does not save; a road that does not lead to truth and life leads nowhere worth going. The Son is what we travel by, what we are travelling to, and the gift that meets us when we arrive. To know any one of these names rightly is to know the other two.

6.author: St. John Chrysostom
6.work: Homilies on the Gospel of St. John, Homily 73
6.text: Chrysostom adds that the disciples have asked for a map and have been given a Person. They wanted to know the way to the Father; the Lord answers, 'I am the way.' No road, no instruction, no creed will do as a substitute. The way is not what Christ teaches but who Christ is. The Christian goes to the Father by being joined to the Son, not by following directions the Son has dictated.

9.author: St. Athanasius the Great
9.text: 'He who has seen Me has seen the Father.' Athanasius hears in this verse the same Nicene confession he made his life defending. The Son is the exact image of the Father, not because He resembles Him as a creature can resemble its Creator, but because He shares the Father's very nature. To see the incarnate Son is to see, as far as flesh can bear it, the Father whom no one can see in His own essence. The Son does not reflect God; He is God.
